Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

please write a practical guide for setting up a volunteer transport rota for the riverside neighbourhood network the guide should cover the first eight weeks of autumn and be usable by the coordinator who is taking over from jo on the first monday in september we have fourteen regular volunteers and usually between nine and sixteen ride requests each week most trips are to the clinic library food pantry or the central bus station make the guide useful to someone who knows the volunteers but has not run this rota before explain how to collect availability and turn it into a schedule without implying that every request can always be covered keep the tone calm and direct and make the steps clear enough that a new coordinator could follow them without asking jo to fill in missing details

describe a weekly rhythm that begins with gathering requests by wednesday afternoon and checking volunteer availability on thursday morning the rota should normally go out by friday at three but the guide should leave room for a later change when a clinic appointment is only confirmed after that point say how to flag an unfilled request without making it look like a confirmed ride and how to contact the person who asked for help before offering another time do not promise that a volunteer will be found explain that the coordinator can ask whether the passenger has another safe way to travel while keeping that question respectful and optional include a simple procedure for a volunteer who needs to cancel after confirming and for the coordinator who has to tell a passenger about a change

in the numbered section use item 1 for checking a new request and item 2 for confirming a ride before it is shared give each item a short sequence of actions that includes checking the pickup window, destination, mobility equipment, and any vehicle or lift requirement before assigning someone item 1 should also mention asking whether the person can manage a short wait if the appointment runs late item 2 should include confirming the volunteer has accepted the trip and knows where to collect the van keys do not make a volunteer responsible for collecting a passenger's medical history and do not include payment or reimbursement rules because the network has not decided those yet keep the two items focused on the rota rather than turning them into a general volunteer handbook

The guide should cover the first eight weeks of autumn and be usable by the coordinator who is taking over from Jo on the first Monday in September. We have fourteen regular volunteers and usually between nine and sixteen ride requests each week. Most trips are to the clinic, library, food pantry, or the central bus station. Make the guide useful to someone who knows the volunteers but has not run this rota before. Explain how to collect availability and turn it into a schedule without implying that every request can always be covered. Keep the tone calm and direct, and make the steps clear enough that a new coordinator could follow them without asking Jo to fill in missing details.

Include the practical limits that affect assignments. Three volunteers can drive wheelchair-accessible vans, and the network has two of those vans. One is kept at the community hall, and the other is shared with the senior lunch program. The lunch program has first use on Tuesdays until noon, and the van keys are kept in a locked box at reception. Six volunteers can carry folding walkers, but only four have current training for the lift at the clinic entrance. Two volunteers prefer not to drive after dark, and one can only take trips inside the Riverside area. Note that volunteers may offer a trip but should not be described as confirmed until the coordinator has checked the vehicle and the passenger details. Explain how to keep these limits visible when requests arrive close to a deadline.

Say that volunteers usually offer blocks of time rather than exact appointments, and that the coordinator should match those blocks with request windows when possible. Mara offered Monday and Thursday mornings and said, “I can take the early loop if someone else covers the clinic return.” Do not turn that quote into a standing promise or assign her a specific passenger without checking first. Include a way to record a volunteer's preferred contact method and whether they are comfortable receiving a same-day call, but do not assume that a person who has not replied is unavailable. Describe how the coordinator can ask a clear follow-up question and give volunteers a reasonable time to answer before the weekly rota is shared.

For any computer work on the rota, do not install packages; use the existing shared spreadsheet and its built-in features. The coordinator may sort rows, add a new tab for each week, and use the formulas already in the file. Do not suggest moving the information into a new service or sending passenger details to a personal account. The spreadsheet currently has columns for request date, pickup window, destination, mobility equipment, vehicle needed, assigned volunteer, confirmation status, and coordinator notes. Explain what information belongs in each relevant column and which details should stay out of general notes. Use initials rather than full passenger names in the rota that all volunteers can see, and keep the contact list in the restricted folder.

Describe a weekly rhythm that begins with gathering requests by Wednesday afternoon and checking volunteer availability on Thursday morning. The rota should normally go out by Friday at three, but the guide should leave room for a later change when a clinic appointment is only confirmed after that point. Say how to flag an unfilled request without making it look like a confirmed ride, and how to contact the person who asked for help before offering another time. Do not promise that a volunteer will be found. Explain that the coordinator can ask whether the passenger has another safe way to travel while keeping that question respectful and optional. Include a simple procedure for a volunteer who needs to cancel after confirming and for the coordinator who has to tell a passenger about a change.

In the numbered section, use Item 1 for checking a new request and Item 2 for confirming a ride before it is shared. Give each item a short sequence of actions that includes checking the pickup window, destination, mobility equipment, and any vehicle or lift requirement before assigning someone. Item 1 should also mention asking whether the person can manage a short wait if the appointment runs late. Item 2 should include confirming the volunteer has accepted the trip and knows where to collect the van keys. Do not make a volunteer responsible for collecting a passenger's medical history, and do not include payment or reimbursement rules because the network has not decided those yet. Keep the two items focused on the rota rather than turning them into a general volunteer handbook.

Include what to do when two requests compete for the same accessible van or when a volunteer's offered time only covers one direction. Describe checking the van calendar and asking whether either trip has a flexible appointment window before changing an assignment. If neither trip can be adjusted, the coordinator should tell both requesters what is still unconfirmed and ask the transport lead to help with next steps. Do not have the guide choose which passenger matters more or present a possible option as a completed booking. Mention that weather, a late clinic visit, or a vehicle fault can disrupt the plan, and that the coordinator should make a fresh check rather than relying on last week's arrangement.

Finish with a brief description of the handover record to leave for the next coordinator after each week. Include which rides were completed, which requests were not covered, any outstanding confirmation, van or key issues, and any volunteer availability changes. Distinguish a canceled ride from a request that was never assigned, and keep the record factual without guessing why someone missed a trip. Say that the next coordinator should know where the current spreadsheet and restricted contact list are stored, but do not include passwords or private passenger details in the handover itself. End with a separate practical note that the community hall reception closes at five on Fridays, so keys for a Saturday trip need to be collected earlier."}]
